audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for apostolic rights, voluntary self-limitation, becoming all things, race/discipline imagery.

verses.restored: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

familiar.text: Am I not an apostle? am I not free? have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? are not ye my work in the Lord?

modern.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?

original.text: Οὐκ εἰμὶ ⸂ἐλεύθερος; οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος⸃; οὐχὶ ⸀Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἑόρακα; οὐ τὸ ἔργον μου ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν κυρίῳ;

verses.restored: If to others I am not an apostle, at least I am to you, for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

familiar.text: If I be not an apostle unto others, yet doubtless I am to you: for the seal of mine apostleship are ye in the Lord.

modern.text: Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

original.text: εἰ ἄλλοις οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος, ἀλλά γε ὑμῖν εἰμι, ἡ γὰρ σφραγίς ⸂μου τῆς⸃ ἀποστολῆς ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν κυρίῳ.

verses.restored: My defense to those examining me is this:

familiar.text: Mine answer to them that do examine me is this,

modern.text: This is my defense to those who scrutinize me:

original.text: Ἡ ἐμὴ ἀπολογία τοῖς ἐμὲ ἀνακρίνουσίν ⸂ἐστιν αὕτη⸃.

verses.restored: Do we not have authority to eat and drink?

familiar.text: Have we not power to eat and to drink?

modern.text: Have we no right to food and to drink?

original.text: μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν φαγεῖν καὶ ⸀πεῖν;

verses.restored: Do we not have authority to take along a believing wife/sister, as also the rest of the apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?

familiar.text: Have we not power to lead about a sister, a wife, as well as other apostles, and as the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?

modern.text: Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?

original.text: μὴ οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν ἀδελφὴν γυναῖκα περιάγειν, ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ Κηφᾶς;

verses.restored: Or only I and Barnabas, do we not have authority to refrain from working?

familiar.text: Or I only and Barnabas, have not we power to forbear working?

modern.text: Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?

original.text: ἢ μόνος ἐγὼ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν ⸀μὴ ἐργάζεσθαι;

verses.restored: Who serves as soldier at one's own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not eat from the milk of the flock?

familiar.text: Who goeth a warfare any time at his own charges? who planteth a vineyard, and eateth not of the fruit thereof? or who feedeth a flock, and eateth not of the milk of the flock?

modern.text: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?

original.text: τίς στρατεύεται ἰδίοις ὀψωνίοις ποτέ; τίς φυτεύει ἀμπελῶνα καὶ ⸂τὸν καρπὸν⸃ αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐσθίει; ⸀τίς ποιμαίνει ποίμνην καὶ ἐκ τοῦ γάλακτος τῆς ποίμνης οὐκ ἐσθίει;

verses.restored: Do I speak these things according to human reasoning? Or does not the Law also say these things?

familiar.text: Say I these things as a man? or saith not the law the same also?

modern.text: Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?

original.text: Μὴ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ταῦτα λαλῶ ἢ ⸂καὶ ὁ νόμος ταῦτα οὐ⸃ λέγει;

verses.restored: For in the Law of Moses it is written: You shall not muzzle an ox treading grain. Is the Divine concerned for oxen only?

familiar.text: For it is written in the law of Moses, Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn. Doth God take care for oxen?

modern.text: For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?

original.text: ἐν γὰρ τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ γέγραπται· Οὐ ⸀κημώσεις βοῦν ἀλοῶντα. μὴ τῶν βοῶν μέλει τῷ θεῷ,

verses.restored: Or does he speak entirely because of us? Because of us it was written, that the one plowing ought to plow in hope, and the one threshing in hope of sharing.

familiar.text: Or saith he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.

modern.text: Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.

original.text: ἢ διʼ ἡμᾶς πάντως λέγει; διʼ ἡμᾶς γὰρ ἐγράφη, ὅτι ⸂ὀφείλει ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι⸃ ὁ ἀροτριῶν ἀροτριᾶν, καὶ ὁ ἀλοῶν ⸂ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι τοῦ μετέχειν⸃.

verses.restored: If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it a great thing if we harvest your material things?

familiar.text: If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things?

modern.text: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?

original.text: εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν τὰ πνευματικὰ ἐσπείραμεν, μέγα εἰ ἡμεῖς ὑμῶν τὰ σαρκικὰ θερίσομεν;

verses.restored: If others share this authority over you, do we not more? But we did not use this authority; rather, we endure all things so that we may give no hindrance to the good news of Messiah.

familiar.text: If others be partakers of this power over you, are not we rather? Nevertheless we have not used this power; but suffer all things, lest we should hinder the gospel of Christ.

modern.text: If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.

original.text: εἰ ἄλλοι τῆς ⸂ὑμῶν ἐξουσίας⸃ μετέχουσιν, οὐ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς; Ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐχρησάμεθα τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ταύτῃ, ἀλλὰ πάντα στέγομεν ἵνα μή ⸂τινα ἐγκοπὴν⸃ δῶμεν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: Do you not know that those working the sacred things eat from the temple, and those attending the altar share with the altar?

familiar.text: Do ye not know that they which minister about holy things live of the things of the temple? and they which wait at the altar are partakers with the altar?

modern.text: Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?

original.text: οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ τὰ ἱερὰ ἐργαζόμενοι ⸀τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ἐσθίουσιν, οἱ τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ⸀παρεδρεύοντες τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ συμμερίζονται;

verses.restored: So also the Lord directed those announcing the good news to live from the good news.

familiar.text: Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel.

modern.text: In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.

original.text: οὕτως καὶ ὁ κύριος διέταξεν τοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον καταγγέλλουσιν ἐκ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ζῆν.

verses.restored: But I have used none of these things. I do not write these things so that it may be done thus in me; for it would be beautiful/good for me rather to die than that anyone empty my boast.

familiar.text: But I have used none of these things: neither have I written these things, that it should be so done unto me: for it were better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void.

modern.text: But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.

original.text: Ἐγὼ δὲ ⸂οὐ κέχρημαι οὐδενὶ⸃ τούτων. οὐκ ἔγραψα δὲ ταῦτα ἵνα οὕτως γένηται ἐν ἐμοί, καλὸν γάρ μοι μᾶλλον ἀποθανεῖν ἤ— τὸ καύχημά μου ⸂οὐδεὶς κενώσει⸃.

verses.restored: For if I announce good news, there is no boast for me; necessity lies upon me, for woe is me if I do not announce good news.

familiar.text: For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!

modern.text: Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!

original.text: ἐὰν γὰρ εὐαγγελίζωμαι, οὐκ ἔστιν μοι καύχημα, ἀνάγκη γάρ μοι ἐπίκειται· οὐαὶ ⸀γάρ μοί ἐστιν ἐὰν μὴ ⸀εὐαγγελίσωμαι.

verses.restored: For if I do this willingly, I have a wage; but if unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship.

familiar.text: For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.

modern.text: If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ἑκὼν τοῦτο πράσσω, μισθὸν ἔχω· εἰ δὲ ἄκων, οἰκονομίαν πεπίστευμαι.

verses.restored: What then is my wage? That announcing good news, I may make the good news without charge, so as not to use fully my authority in the good news.

familiar.text: What is my reward then? Verily that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel.

modern.text: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it. Paul the Servant to All

original.text: τίς οὖν ⸀μού ἐστιν ὁ μισθός; ἵνα εὐαγγελιζόμενος ἀδάπανον θήσω τὸ ⸀εὐαγγέλιον, εἰς τὸ μὴ καταχρήσασθαι τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.

verses.restored: For being free from all, I enslaved myself to all, so that I might gain the more.

familiar.text: For though I be free from all men, yet have I made myself servant unto all, that I might gain the more.

modern.text: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.

original.text: Ἐλεύθερος γὰρ ὢν ἐκ πάντων πᾶσιν ἐμαυτὸν ἐδούλωσα, ἵνα τοὺς πλείονας κερδήσω·

verses.restored: To Judeans I became as Judean, so that I might gain Judeans; to those under Law as under Law, though not myself being under Law, so that I might gain those under Law.

familiar.text: And unto the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain the Jews; to them that are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain them that are under the law;

modern.text: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.

original.text: καὶ ἐγενόμην τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὡς Ἰουδαῖος, ἵνα Ἰουδαίους κερδήσω· τοῖς ὑπὸ νόμον ὡς ὑπὸ νόμον, ⸂μὴ ὢν αὐτὸς ὑπὸ νόμον⸃, ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον κερδήσω·

verses.restored: To those without Law as without Law, not being without Divine law but within Messiah's law, so that I might gain those without Law.

familiar.text: To them that are without law, as without law, (being not without law to God, but under the law to Christ,) that I might gain them that are without law.

modern.text: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.

original.text: τοῖς ἀνόμοις ὡς ἄνομος, μὴ ὢν ἄνομος ⸀θεοῦ ἀλλʼ ἔννομος ⸀Χριστοῦ, ἵνα ⸀κερδάνω ⸀τοὺς ἀνόμους·

verses.restored: To the weak I became weak, so that I might gain the weak. To all I have become all things, so that by all means I might save/heal some.

familiar.text: To the weak became I as weak, that I might gain the weak: I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some.

modern.text: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.

original.text: ἐγενόμην τοῖς ⸀ἀσθενέσιν ἀσθενής, ἵνα τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς κερδήσω· τοῖς πᾶσιν ⸀γέγονα πάντα, ἵνα πάντως τινὰς σώσω.

verses.restored: I do all things because of the good news, so that I may become a sharer with it.

familiar.text: And this I do for the gospel’s sake, that I might be partaker thereof with you.

modern.text: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings. Run Your Race to Win

original.text: ⸀πάντα δὲ ποιῶ διὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, ἵνα συγκοινωνὸς αὐτοῦ γένωμαι.

verses.restored: Do you not know that those running in a stadium all run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may take hold.

familiar.text: Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.

modern.text: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.

original.text: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἐν σταδίῳ τρέχοντες πάντες μὲν τρέχουσιν, εἷς δὲ λαμβάνει τὸ βραβεῖον; οὕτως τρέχετε ἵνα καταλάβητε.

verses.restored: Everyone competing exercises self-control in all things; they do it to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable.

familiar.text: And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.

modern.text: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.

original.text: πᾶς δὲ ὁ ἀγωνιζόμενος πάντα ἐγκρατεύεται, ἐκεῖνοι μὲν οὖν ἵνα φθαρτὸν στέφανον λάβωσιν, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄφθαρτον.

verses.restored: Therefore I run this way, not uncertainly; I box this way, not beating air.

familiar.text: I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air:

modern.text: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.

original.text: ἐγὼ τοίνυν οὕτως τρέχω ὡς οὐκ ἀδήλως, οὕτως πυκτεύω ὡς οὐκ ἀέρα δέρων·

verses.restored: But I discipline my body and make it a servant, lest somehow, after proclaiming to others, I myself should become disapproved.

familiar.text: But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.

modern.text: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ὑπωπιάζω μου τὸ σῶμα καὶ δουλαγωγῶ, μή πως ἄλλοις κηρύξας αὐτὸς ἀδόκιμος γένωμαι.

translation_notes: Paul's freedom is expressed through voluntary self-limitation for the good news, not through domination.
Athletic imagery is discipline for service, not body-hatred.
